newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett-Packard sets $1 billion share buyback.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard sets $1 billion share buyback.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co. said Friday its board of directors authorised the repurchase of an additional $1 billion of common stock and two new executive appointments.
The Palo Alto-based maker of computers, printers and other computer equipment said the board had approved the share buyback on the open market but did not set a date for completing the repurchases.
About $230 million remains from earlier authorisations, the company said, bringing the current outstanding total in authorised amounts for repurchasing shares to $1.23 billion.
Hewlett-Packard rose $1 to close at $54.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Since the start of 1994, Hewlett-Packard has repurchased 61.5 million shares, the company said. At current prices, the authorisation would cover the purchase of roughly 23 million shares.

Hewlett-Packard said on Monday that earnings for its 1996 fiscal year rose 6 percent to $2.6 billion, or $2.46 a share, from $2.4 billion, or $2.31 a share in fiscal 1995 as sales rose 22 percent to $38.4 billion from $31.5 billion.
Hewlett-Packard also said its board had elected Edward Barnholt as executive vice president and John Scruggs to the position of vice president.
Barnholt, 53, heads the test and measurement organisation, which is responsible for design, manufacturing, marketing, sales and support of HP instruments and systems.

Scruggs, 55, is general manager of HP's automated test group, which has worldwide responsibility for providing highly integrated systems and associated services for testing semiconductor components and electronic assemblies.
